rationale: Evidence from iteration 7 (score 933.8, the best so far) and iteration 8 (score 930.8). Iteration 7 has oval 20/20 (2.37 s, rms 0.0055), s-bend 20/20 (2.53 s, rms 0.013) and slalom 19/20 (one timeout, 0 off-track exits, mean progress 0.995). Iteration 8 raised base_speed to 1.0. Its slalom regressed (one off-track exit, minimum score 308, mean 904 against 911), and its oval and s-bend gained only about 0.03 to 0.04 s. Raising speed therefore brings slalom instability without a clear time gain, so base_speed goes back to 0.95. The score's remaining lever on the oval and s-bend is completion time (60*(1-t/3)), and the main loss is the single slalom failure. The slalom's problem is steering authority at fast reversals, which is the limit named in iteration 7's hypothesis (2). Change (single variable from iteration 7): wheel_track 0.11 -> 0.10 m. For the same wheel differential, a narrower track gives a higher turn rate, so the robot can correct reversals faster without raising speed. Everything else is held at iteration 7: seven sensors at x = -0.04..+0.04 m (0.0133 m pitch), sensor_size 0.012, weights 50*x, kp 4.5, ki 0, kd 3.0, base_speed 0.95, mass 0.6, body 0.15 x 0.12 m, radius 0.03 m, line_loss last_direction. Expected result: slalom 20/20 with fewer timeouts and off-track exits, and oval and s-bend still finishing with rms under 0.015. Hypotheses: (1) if the s-bend or oval steering_oscillation rises above 0.25, or rms rises above 0.015, the narrower track is overturning and should return to 0.11 m or the kd should rise to 3.3; (2) if the slalom still times out at progress near 0.99, the limit is speed, so base_speed should go to 0.975 with wheel_track 0.10; (3) if the slalom leaves the tape, kd should rise to 3.5 before changing speed. Measurements requested: all metrics per track, with focus on slalom finish count, timeouts versus off-track exits, completion_time on the oval and s-bend, and steering_oscillation.
